---
title: "Lecture notes"
subtitle: "Guided explanations, examples, questions, and in-class activities"
---

Lecture pages are the main narrative course materials. They are designed to move from one idea to the next like a class meeting: a motivating claim, a concrete example, an explanation, a checkpoint, and an opportunity to apply the idea.

Computational work lives separately in the [notebooks](../notebooks/index.qmd). A lecture may link to a notebook when running code or collecting evidence materially improves the lesson, but the lecture itself should remain readable without a computational environment.

## Week 1

- [Is a database just a glorified spreadsheet?](week-01-database-or-spreadsheet.qmd) — Where tabular files work, where they break, and what keys, relationships, constraints, and transactions add.

## Planned organization

Each lecture page will generally include:

1. a motivating question or claim;
2. explicit learning goals;
3. short, visually separated topics;
4. diagrams and worked examples;
5. prediction or discussion checkpoints; and
6. a brief activity or exit ticket.
